title: Effective etale descent for polarized schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For each $i$ let $X_i\to U_i$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme] and let $L_i$ be an invertible module on $X_i$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that on $U_i\times_S U_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product] there are isomorphisms $X_i\times_{U_i}(U_i\times_S U_j)\simeq X_j\times_{U_j}(U_i\times_S U_j)$ satisfying identity and cocycle conditions, and isomorphisms $\lambda_{ij}:\theta_{ij}^*L_j\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i$ on the corresponding scheme overlaps, where $\theta_{ij}$ denotes the specified scheme isomorphism. Require the identity condition for $\lambda_{ii}$ after restriction along the diagonal $U_i\to U_i\times_SU_i$, and the cocycle condition $\lambda_{ik}=\lambda_{ij}\circ\theta_{ij}^*\lambda_{jk}$ on every triple overlap, using $\theta_{jk}\circ\theta_{ij}=\theta_{ik}$ to identify their domains. Assume that for every affine open $V\subset U_i$, the restriction of $L_i$ to $X_i\times_{U_i}V$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there exist a scheme $X\to S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an invertible module $L$ on $X$, with compatible isomorphisms $(X,L)\times_S U_i\simeq(X_i,L_i)$. The descended pair is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), Tag 02WW (spaces theorem-presentation), Tag 04W8 (fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules), and the scheme case of Descent Tag 023Q.

proof.text: Form the schemes $V=\coprod_iX_i$ and $R=\coprod_{i,j}R_{ij}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], where $R_{ij}=X_i\times_{U_i}(U_i\times_SU_j)$. Its source is projection to $X_i$; its target is projection to $X_j$ after $\theta_{ij}$. The source on $R_{ij}$ is a base change of $U_j\to S$, and the target is, up to $\theta_{ij}$, a base change of $U_i\to S$. Thus they are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Their coproducts are etale: the summands are open and cover the source, so the affine-local definition of [def-weil-etale-morphism] checks this on each summand. The map $R\to V\times_SV$ is a monomorphism: two arrows with specified source and target have the same indices locally, the same two base maps to $U_i,U_j$, and the same $X_i$-map, hence the same map to $R_{ij}$ by the fibre-product universal property. The identity along the diagonal gives reflexivity. The cocycle with indices $(i,j,i)$ gives the inverse, and the general cocycle gives composition. These checks apply after decomposing any test scheme into the opens on which the summand indices are fixed. Consequently this is an etale equivalence relation over $S$.

source.place: Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation), construction of its input from the given datum; affine-local etaleness and the stated identity/cocycle conditions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to the relation just constructed. Write $F=V/R$ for its algebraic-space quotient and $q:V\to F$ for the etale surjective atlas. It has $V\times_FV=R$. Since both arrows of $R$ are over $S$, the quotient is an algebraic space over $S$. All subsequent fibre products and line modules on $F$ use [def-trf-algebraic-space].

The map $X_i\to F$ and its structure map to $U_i$ give $a_i:h_{X_i}\to F\times_Sh_{U_i}$. To prove $a_i$ invertible, fix a test scheme $T\to U_i$ and a section $z\in F(T)$. By [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], $z$ lifts etale locally on $T$ to $V$. Refining by the open summands of $V$, write each lift as $x_j:T_a\to X_j$, and let $u_j:T_a\to U_j$ be its base. Apply $\theta_{ji}$ with the pair $(u_j,u_i)$ to get $y_a:T_a\to X_i$. On $T_a\times_TT_b$, the two lifts form a section of $R=V\times_FV$, so they are related by the specified $\theta_{jk}$. The cocycle gives $\theta_{ki}\theta_{jk}=\theta_{ji}$ and hence equality of the resulting maps to $X_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], applied on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ to the scheme $T\times_{U_i}X_i$, these maps glue uniquely to $y:T\to X_i$. Conversely, two maps to $X_i$ with the same $F$-image give an $R_{ii}$-arrow whose two base maps to $U_i$ agree. This arrow restricts along the diagonal, where $\theta_{ii}$ is the identity, so the maps are equal. The construction commutes with restriction of $T$ and is inverse to $a_i$. Thus $F\times_SU_i\simeq X_i$, with overlap identifications exactly $\theta_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 02WW, presentation kernel pair; explicit cocycle calculation and representable sheaf gluing.

proof.text: The family $X_i\to F$ is an etale covering: it is the atlas $V\to F$ restricted to its open summands. Under $X_i\times_FX_j=R_{ij}$, the given $\lambda_{ij}$ is an isomorphism from the pullback of $L_j$ by the target to the pullback of $L_i$ by the source. Its diagonal identity and triple-overlap cocycle are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent]. That lemma therefore gives a line module $L$ on $F$ and identifications with the ordinary invertible modules $L_i$ inducing every specified $\lambda_{ij}$.

Use [lem-trf-algebraic-space-ample-local] for $F\to S$, the line module $L$, and the given etale covering $U_i\to S$. The previous identifications make its base changes exactly $(X_i,L_i)$, and the restriction of $L_i$ to every inverse image of an affine open in $U_i$ is ample by hypothesis. Hence $F\to S$ is representable. Testing representability on $S\to S$ shows that $F$ itself is a scheme $X$. The restriction of $L$ is an ordinary invertible module on $X$ by the scheme-site interpretation in [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent]. This gives the required pair and all specified descent identifications.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), together with Divisors on Spaces Tag 0D36 (lemma-relatively-ample-local).

proof.text: Let $(X,L)$ and $(X',L')$ be two pairs with the specified identifications. Over $X\times_SU_i\simeq X_i$ define the map to $X'$ by the prescribed identification with $X'\times_SU_i$, followed by projection. The scheme cocycle says these maps agree on every double overlap. This family is an etale covering of $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], so [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] gives a unique scheme map $b:X\to X'$. Interchanging the two pairs gives an inverse: each composite restricts to the identity on every member of the cover, hence equals the identity by uniqueness in that same sheaf condition. The prescribed local isomorphisms $b^*L'\simeq L$ agree on the overlaps because both pairs induce $\lambda_{ij}$. Full faithfulness in [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent] glues them to a unique module map, and glues their inverses; the composites are identities by faithfulness. Thus there is exactly one compatible isomorphism of pairs.
